The Under 12.0 at LowVig is priced at +101 against a median of -110 — a massive 263 edge_bps gap, the largest on the entire board today. Coors Field games routinely inflate totals, but getting plus-money on the under at a 12-run number with Merrill Kelly (a reliable ground-ball arm) going for Arizona is exceptional line value. This is a direct pricing inefficiency at LowVig versus the rest of the market, and the +101 represents real edge that should be captured immediately.

BetRivers is posting Guardians -1.5 at +170 while the median across all nine books is +157 — a 187 edge_bps gap that stands out as one of the cleaner spread inefficiencies on the slate. The +170 at BetRivers is a full 13 cents better than median, making this a high-value play.

Edward Cabrera starts for the Cubs against Sean Burke for the White Sox; the White Sox continue to be one of the worst offensive clubs in baseball, and the Cubs are significantly the better team here. Getting +122 on a Cubs run-line against Chicago's hapless offense with a quality arm going is excellent value, and the price discrepancy confirms this is mispriced at LowVig.

The Under 9.0 at BetMGM sits at -118 against a median of -125 across six books — a 143 edge_bps gap. Shane Baz takes the hill for Baltimore against Zack Littell for Washington; both pitchers have shown the ability to keep games close, and a total of 9.0 for a Nationals home game feels inflated. The best price on the market at -118 (7 cents better than median) makes BetMGM the clear play here.

LowVig.ag has the Timberwolves +5.0 at -103 versus a median of -108 across six books — a 118 edge_bps edge. The Spurs are listed as heavy favorites on the moneyline (-188 to -210 range), but getting Minnesota plus five at nearly even money is valuable considering the Wolves are competitive at home and the line movement from 4.5 to 5.5 across books shows disagreement in the market. The -103 price at LowVig is the sharpest available on the dominant line.

BetRivers is posting Over 6.5 at +108 against a median of +101 — a 167 edge_bps gap and the only plus-money over on this line. The Canadiens are moderate home favorites (-155 to -167), and Montreal-Buffalo matchups in hockey tend to be up-tempo affairs. Getting plus-money on the over in a game where both teams have offensive incentive (Montreal at home, Buffalo fighting for positioning) represents genuine market value at BetRivers.

ig_carousel_topic.topic: CLV (closing line value) and why sharps obsess over it
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Why do sharp bettors care more about the closing line than the final score?
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors check one thing: did the bet win?
Sharps check something different.
They check where the line closed versus where they got on.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
The closing line is the market's best estimate of true probability.
Thousands of dollars and sharp action move it all week.
If you beat that number, you had an edge. Full stop. The result is noise.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
You bet the Over at -105. It closes at -118.
You beat the closing line by 13 cents.
Over a large sample, that gap compounds into real profit regardless of any single outcome.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Win rate lies in small samples. Closing line value doesn't.
Track your CLV. It tells you whether your process is working before your record does.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: CLV is the metric serious bettors track. Not win rate, not units on a hot week. This is what the closing line actually tells you.
